Wedding Ceremony of Nick Plewtong and Tiffany Prather 
Dear friends and family, welcome! We are gathered here today in beautiful Monterey right on the Pacific Ocean to share in the celebration of the joining of Nick and Tiffany in a union of matrimony and to wish them well on this joyous occasion. Their time of over 8 years together has developed into a love and understanding in which the two have come, surrounded by their family and friends in the midst of these picturesque surroundings to affirm their commitment to each other.
Definition of Marriage
Marriage is a commitment to life, to the best that two people can find and bring out in each other. It offers opportunities for sharing and growth that no other human relationship can equal; a joining that is promised for a lifetime. Within the circle of its love, marriage encompasses all of life’s most important relationships. A wife and a husband are each other’s best friend, confidant, lover, teacher, listener, and critic. Marriage deepens and enriches every facet of life. Happiness is fuller; memories are fresher; commitment is stronger; even anger is felt more strongly and passes away more quickly. Marriage understands and forgives the mistakes life is unable to avoid. It encourages and nurtures new life, new experiences, and new ways of expressing love through the seasons of life. When two people pledge to love and care for each other in marriage, they create a spirit unique to themselves, which binds them closer than any spoken or written words. Marriage is a promise, a potential, made in the hearts of two people who love, which takes a lifetime to fulfill. By Edmund O’Neill
Introduction
Today is the beginning of a beautiful adventure for this couple. Drawing on their mutual admiration and respect for one another, they are ready to embark on a new voyage together. Marriage symbolizes the intimate sharing of two lives. It is the development of a balanced relationship that is continually growing and changing. Nick and Tiffany met in their first year at Cal Poly through playing intramural sports. It turns out that there are some things you can't share without ending up liking each other, and playing Futsal together is one of them. After months of friendship and discovering a mutual love for Disney, they began officially dating. As they navigated the college experience and obtained degrees in Engineering and Computer Science, they learned and grew together as individuals and as a couple. Ecclesiastes 4 speaks to the importance of having a partner in life:
Two are better than one,
    because they have a good return for their labor: 
If either of them falls down,
    one can help the other up.
But pity anyone who falls
    and has no one to help them up. 
Also, if two lie down together, they will keep warm.
    But how can one keep warm alone? 
Though one may be overpowered,
    two can defend themselves.

Nick and Tiffany have demonstrated their support and love for each other as partners throughout school and beyond - from Tiffany always attending Nick’s violin performances, to helping each other with computer science work, to exploring their love of food and travel together. They have since conquered many challenges, such as adopting two adorable kitties and running marathons at Disney World. I am so fortunate to call them both dear friends with whom I had the pleasure of spending most of my college years and I couldn’t be happier than to have the privilege of marrying them today.
Nick and Tiffany, the promises you make today are the groundwork from which your marriage will grow and blossom over time. As individuals, we make the choice to enter the union of marriage in order to share all aspects of ourselves with our soulmate. For Nick and Tiffany, one of the happiest things they share is their fondness of Disney. Beyond being the most magical place on earth, I think one of the greatest things that Disney symbolizes for many is possibilities: the possibility of love, of adventure, and of finding your happily ever after.
Finding someone with whom to share that happily ever after is surely one of life’s greatest treasures. In that spirit, the mother of the bride Julie will now share a short passage on the beauty of love from 1st Corinthians: 


Mother of Bride Reading
4 Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud. 5 It does not dishonor others, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no record of wrongs. 6 Love does not delight in evil but rejoices with the truth. 7 It always protects, always trusts, always hopes, always perseveres.


The love that Paul speaks of in this piece of scripture is aspirational. Having witnessed their love story blossom over time, I know that Nick and Tiffany are well poised to share this kind of love in their life and marriage. Together, let us take a moment to acknowledge the gravity of the commitment being entered into today. 


Nick & Tiffany Vows


I now invite the couple to share their vows with one another. Nick, would you like to begin?
Nick Vows
Tiffany, your turn.
Tiffany Vows
Nick and Tiffany, the promises you make today are the groundwork from which your marriage will grow and blossom over time. The contract of marriage is not to be taken lightly, but thoughtfully and seriously, with a deep realization of its obligations and responsibilities. 
Wedding Vows
Nick and Tiffany, please join hands.
Nick, Do you take Tiffany for your lawful wife, to have and to hold, from this day forward, for better or for worse, for richer or for poorer, in sickness and in health, until death do you part?  Nick: I do 

Tiffany, Do you take Nick for your lawful husband, to have and to hold, from this day forward, for better or for worse, for richer or for poorer, in sickness and in health, until death do you part? Tiffany: I do 

Nick and Tiffany, have you come here to enter into marriage without coercion, freely and wholeheartedly? Are you prepared, as you follow the path of Marriage, to love and to honor each other for as long as you both shall live? Both: We do
Exchange of Rings
Today you will be exchanging rings as a symbol of the everlasting love that you two share. They are set in a circle around your finger with no end or beginning to illustrate your eternal commitment to each other. Nick, are you ready?

Nick, please place and hold the ring on the ring finger of Tiffany’s left hand and repeat after me
 
Tiffany, with this ring, I thee wed repeat 
It is a symbol of my never-ending love for you repeat 
and a sign of my commitment to you repeat 

Tiffany, please place and hold the ring on the ring finger of Nick’s left hand and repeat after me 

Nick, with this ring, I thee wed repeat 
It is a symbol of my never-ending love for you repeat 
and a sign of my commitment to you repeat 

Closing:

May your marriage bring you all the exquisite excitements a marriage should bring, and may life grant you also patience, tolerance, and understanding. 
May you always need one another, not so much to fill your emptiness as to help you to know your fullness. 
May you succeed in all-important ways with one another, and not fail in the little graces. 
May you look for things to praise, often say, "I love you!" and take no notice of small faults. 
May you have happiness, and may you find it making one another happy. 
May you have love, and may you find it loving one another.
 	By James Dillet Freeman
Nick and Tiffany, just remember:
Marriage is a promise, made in the hearts of two people who love, which takes a lifetime to fulfill.

Nick and Tiffany, by the power vested in me, on behalf of all those present, and by the strength of your own love, I now pronounce you married, husband and wife. 

STEP TO THE SIDE

Nick, you may kiss the bride.
 
KISS

Ladies and gentlemen, at this time it is my pleasure to present to you for the first time ever, Mr. and Mrs. Plewtong!
